worktree_state.content:
# Database (Neon)
DATABASE_URL="postgres://user:password@endpoint.neon.tech/neondb?sslmode=require"

# Authentication (Lucia)
# No specific env needed for basic Lucia with Argon2, but strict session cookies need HTTPS in prod.
NODE_ENV="development"

# Google Cloud Storage (Service Account JSON or specific fields)
# GCS_CREDENTIALS="{...}" or path to file
GCS_PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
GCS_BUCKET_NAME="your-bucket-name"
GCS_CLIENT_EMAIL="your-service-account-email"
GCS_PRIVATE_KEY="your-private-key"

# AI Provider Keys (Optional for server if stored in DB, but good for defaults)
GEMINI_API_KEY=""
OPENAI_API_KEY=""

# ===================================================================
# Security Configuration (Content Security Policy)
# ===================================================================

# CSP_ENABLED - Enable or disable Content Security Policy headers
# Set to "false" to disable CSP entirely (not recommended in production)
# Default: true (CSP enabled)
# Examples: "true" | "false"
CSP_ENABLED="true"

# CSP_MODE - CSP enforcement mode
# - "enforce": Block violations and enforce policy (recommended for production)
# - "report-only": Log violations without blocking (recommended for testing/staging)
# Default: "enforce"
# Examples: "enforce" | "report-only"
CSP_MODE="enforce"

# CSP_REPORT_URI - Endpoint for CSP violation reports
# Optional: If set, browsers will POST JSON violation reports to this URI
# Useful for monitoring CSP violations in production
# Can be a relative path (e.g., "/api/csp-report") or full URL
# Default: undefined (no reporting)
# Examples: "/api/csp-report" | "https://yourdomain.com/api/csp-report"
# CSP_REPORT_URI=""

# Note: NODE_ENV (configured above) determines which CSP policy is used:
# - "development": Permissive policy with 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' for Vite HMR
# - "production": Strict policy with no unsafe directives for maximum XSS protection

task_intent.title: Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) Headers
task_intent.description: Add comprehensive Content Security Policy headers to protect against XSS attacks while allowing the application to function with external AI services and dynamic content.
